info.name: Expense Tracker API
info.description:
REST API for the Expense Tracker backend (Express + TypeScript + TypeORM + PostgreSQL).

## Setup
1. Import this collection and the **Expense Tracker - Local** environment, then select the environment.
2. Start the backend (`cd backend && npm run dev`). It listens on `http://localhost:8080/api`.
3. Run **Auth → Register** (first time) or **Auth → Login**.

## Authentication (HTTP-only cookie)
The API does not use an `Authorization` header. Login and register respond with
`Set-Cookie: access_token=<JWT>; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax`. Postman saves that cookie in its
**cookie jar** and automatically sends it on every later request to `localhost`, the same way a
browser would. That is why the collection auth type is **No Auth**, and no token is ever copied
into a header, body or variable. Logout clears the cookie.

## Running everything
Use **Run collection** (or `npx newman run ...`). Folders run top to bottom and pass IDs along
via collection variables (`categoryId`, `expenseId`, ...). The whole collection can be re-run.

## Adding endpoints
One folder per route module (matching `backend/src/routes/*.routes.ts`). Put requests that
need data from earlier ones after them, save IDs with `pm.collectionVariables.set(...)`, and
rely on the collection-level tests for the shared JSON and error-format checks.

item.name: Auth
item.description:
Registration, login, logout and the current user.

Login/register respond with `Set-Cookie: access_token=...; HttpOnly`. Postman stores it in its cookie jar and sends it with every later request to the same host, exactly like a browser. No token is ever copied by hand.

Order when run top to bottom: register → logout → confirm logged out → login → confirm logged in. It ends logged in so the following folders work.

request.description:
Creates an account and logs it in (sets the auth cookie).

Returns **409** if the email is already registered. The test accepts that too, so the collection can be re-run.

request.description: Clears the auth cookie. Always returns **204**, even if not logged in.

item.name: Categories
item.description:
CRUD for the logged-in user's categories. Requires login (run **Auth → Login** first).

`Create category` saves `categoryId`, which later requests (and the Expenses folder) use. Names include `{{$timestamp}}` so re-running never hits the duplicate-name rule.

response.name: 409 Duplicate name

request.description: All of the user's categories, sorted by name.
Returns **404** if the category does not exist *or belongs to another user*.
Creates a throwaway category for **Delete category**, so the main `categoryId` stays usable for expenses.
Returns **204**. Returns **409** if expenses still use the category.

response.name: 409 Category has expenses

item.name: Expenses
item.description:
CRUD for the logged-in user's expenses, with pagination, filters and search. Requires login and `categoryId` (run **Categories → Create category** first).

`{{today}}`, `{{monthStart}}` and `{{currentMonth}}` are set automatically by the collection pre-request script.
